dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: A—Are you a living person or a ghost?

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: If you are alive as well, then please, help me look for something...

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: I'm looking for... I'm looking for my son...

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: My son is a samurai of the Shogunate. He fought here once, and he...

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: Oh, that's not correct... I remember now. I'm not here for my son. I'm here for the personal items he left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: He died on the battlefield, so he must have left something here. That's why I'm here, looking for them.

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: Yes, there has gotta be something... Even though war is merciless, surely the earth will keep some traces of my son's existence...

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: *sigh* Thank you, youngster. Please take care as well. Don't get yourself involved in some meaningless war...

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: I was a Shogunate soldier when I was young. Fortunately, I was never involved in any major conflicts. That's how I got to retire safely, get married and have kids...

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: It seems that my son was not so fortunate.

dialogues.speaker: Utsumi
dialogues.text: I often wonder — if I hadn't been a samurai, my son would likely not have taken the same path as me. Then he wouldn't have...
